Relationship is a much more well defined concept in corp than in LLC. I don't think entityType is a good mapping for it. Entity type describes the legal structure of the entity rather than how they relate to the issuer. LLC's closest concept is holder "groups", but these are not always a 1:1 mapping with relationships (though in some cases they are). Groups are customizable by the issuers and are mostly used for cap table views and waterfalls as far as I know. There is also no indication on the LLC side that creating a "group" means you are defining a relationship to the issuer. You're more defining a relationship with the other members of the group. This may be another one that we need to punt on, I don't think the concepts match up well.

Does having a lastModifiedDate make sense for LLCs Interest API cc:

On the Design Document another question came up: Would we be able to include a `lastModifiedDate` field in the `Interest` message, and would we be able to add a query filter that allows users to filter by last modified date? To Chet's point, what we see from consumers is that they do a one-time sync for the data, and then run period re-syncing to get updates. Without a `lastModifiedDate` filter, consumers are forced to "sync the world" and sort out what has changed on the client side. If we give the `lastModifiedDate` query filter, then we can greatly reduce the volume of information they have to process. This query parameter should likely be mutually exclusive of the `asOfDateTime` query parameter because I imagine it would be hard for us to return results such as: "Give me interests as of Jan 1, 2023 with last modified date (as of that time) on Nov 1, 2024." From the existing < we get the quantities from the `INTEREST_QUANTITY_BY_DATE` table using the given `asOfDate` and checking if its within the `INTEREST_QUANTITY_BY_DATE.EFFECTIVE_DATE_RANGE` . Since we require the `asOfDate` to populate the quantities I don't see how this can be mutually exclusive. I just wanted to ask if this is a use case we should be considering and if you could give me more context as to how we would come up with the quantities in that event.

Hmm, yeah using last modified is a bit awkward. "As of" dates are definitely required once you get into llc-core but I suppose you could make the argument that if we default the as of date to `now` and include "last modified time" in the query it would work. I think I would be more concerned about the usability from a user perspective, those 2 parameters sound very similar and could be easily confused
So I think they can be considered "mutually exclusive" from the user's perspective, but from llc's perspective if we have a "last modified time" filter we just default to using "now"

Actually was just thinking about it some more and using last modified might get us into some weird edge cases based on how we query for interests. Say for example today is 1/1. We issued an interest with 100 units effective 1/1. We query the API and get back that interest - that's all good. Now we create a new transaction, maybe a repurchase, effective 2/1. We query the API using today's as of date (1/1) and the last modified time is the time when we did our first query. The `interest quantity by date` table would have been updated to reflect the fact that the new date range for our issuance event is from 1/1 to 2/1 - this constitutes an "update". But in reality, as of 1/1 nothing has changed and we would have sent back the same object. This could potentially cause some confusion
if we have a "last modified time" filter we just default to using "now" So if we go this route we would return something like "Invalid Input" when the user enters both `lastModified` and `asOfDate`

Another thing is that if we default the asOfDate to `now` in the general scenario of syncing data at a later date wouldn't we almost always returning new data to the user. Using your example: On 1/1. We issue an interest with 100 units effective 1/1. We query the API and get back that interest. Now we create a new transaction, maybe a repurchase, effective 2/1. The next day 2/1. We query the API for modified records with the last modified time as the time when we did our first query and *llc-core defaults the asOfDate to (2/1)*. Here because we default to a new asOfDate we are returning quantities once a day has passed and the `lastModified` parameter doesn't make sense.

Another thing to consider is the `INTEREST_QUANTITY_BY_DATE` table does not have a last_modified_at / updated field on it. Audrey was able to help me understand that this table is populated by a cron job `InterestQuantityByDateBackfillQuartzJob` which clears the previous records for the interests. That was also why I asked if there was any more information on how we would come up with the quantities for an asOfDate when given a LastModifiedDate.
Ah, yeah it doesn't have update/modified time because the rows are intended to be immutable, it does have a `created` timestamp though which we could use.
Yes, we can check that `lastModified created` for this table. We could be returning all interests anyway if this job is run frequently (once a day). I don't know how its scheduled
